- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been trending sharply upward for 5+ days, model often fails to revert; forecast should be slightly below recent high.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment periods; add 2-5% buffer if sentiment > 0.7.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; sentiment history should be averaged over 3–5 days for robust correction.
